text: We evaluated confidence regularization on the student's predictions in the ANLI testbed, measuring a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.7 across num_seeds = 4 seeds. This is the only outcome measure available for the run, and it should be read with several caveats. No baseline PGR was provided, so we cannot characterize this value as an improvement over any comparison method, nor can we say whether an unregularized student would land above or below it. No standard error or per-seed spread was reported, so the variability of the 0.7 figure is unknown, and with only four seeds the estimate rests on a small sample that cannot support strong claims about stability across random initializations. The result is therefore best treated as a preliminary single-configuration observation on ANLI: confidence regularization yields a PGR of 0.7 under the conditions tested. Establishing whether this reflects a genuine effect would require a matched baseline, reported seed-level variance, and additional seeds.
